title: How Blue Holes Work
summary: Josh and Chuck explain blue holes: deep, dark, roughly circular holes in the sea floor or landlocked, formed as flooded sinkholes in karst limestone when sea levels rose. They cover the Great Blue Hole off Belize (popularized by Jacques Cousteau in 1972), speleothems found there suggesting it was once dry land, tilted stalactites hinting at tectonic shifts, sediment records of hurricanes and dust storms, sea level rise records (rapid rises of about 25 and 21 feet), the toxic hydrogen sulfide layer and its archaea, the conch and hermit crab graveyard, Green Banana Blue Hole in the Gulf of Mexico with its unusual life, possible links to Florida aquifers and Miami saltwater intrusion, the Yongle Blue Hole as the deepest, and the dangers of cave, technical and free diving, including Herbert Nitsch's breath-hold records and the death of Nicholas Mevoli. The episode ends with a listener mail about a father's role as a stringer at Ole Miss during James Meredith's integration, with Dan Rather.

entities.name: The Undersea World of Jacques Cousteau

segments.title: Intro and defining blue holes
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck open with banter about past coverage of caves and sinkholes, then describe blue holes as dark, often circular holes in the sea floor that are popular diving and fishing spots.

segments.title: Great Blue Hole and Jacques Cousteau
segments.summary: The Great Blue Hole off Belize was popularized by Jacques Cousteau's 1972 episode. Blue holes are underwater sinkholes in karst limestone, and they can be landlocked as well as undersea.

segments.title: Speleothems and formation as flooded caves
segments.summary: Stalactites and stalagmites found in blue holes show they were once dry caves before sea levels rose. Tilted formations suggest tectonic shifts.

segments.title: Expedition and deaths in the Great Blue Hole
segments.summary: A National Geographic and Richard Branson expedition mapped the Great Blue Hole in 3D and found debris and human and animal remains. The authorities left the remains in place, which is customary in cave diving.

segments.title: Landlocked blue holes and the sea level history
segments.summary: Landlocked blue holes such as Ankiellen pool are noted. The Great Blue Hole was dry about 26,000 years ago, and rising seas have since submerged it.

segments.title: Paleoclimate and sea level records from blue holes
segments.summary: Sediment in blue holes records ancient hurricanes, drought and dust storms, and radiocarbon-dated speleothems reveal past sea levels, including rapid rises of about 25 and 21 feet.

segments.title: Hydrogen sulfide layer, archaea and life
segments.summary: A toxic hydrogen sulfide layer around 90 meters deep blocks oxygen and creates an anaerobic zone. Archaea live there and digest organic matter. The Great Blue Hole's bottom holds a conch and hermit crab graveyard.

segments.title: Green Banana Blue Hole and Florida aquifers
segments.summary: Green Banana Blue Hole in the Gulf of Mexico is unusually alive, with a two-way nutrient flow, and microbes that convert carbon. Researchers are studying links to Florida aquifers and saltwater intrusion affecting Miami.

segments.title: Largest and deepest blue holes and diving dangers
segments.summary: The Yongle Blue Hole in the South China Sea is the deepest, and the Great Blue Hole is the largest by combined width and depth. Diving is dangerous, involving technical and cave diving, nitrogen narcosis, and hydrogen sulfide.

segments.title: Free diving records and deaths
segments.summary: No limits free diving is discussed, with Herbert Nitsch's unofficial 831-foot record and the 2012 death of Nicholas Mevoli at a Vertical Blue competition at Dean's Blue Hole. Divers in Dean's Blue Hole and an Egyptian blue hole were also mentioned.

segments.title: Listener mail: Dan Rather and Ole Miss
segments.summary: A listener, Brenda, shares her father's story of stringing audio for networks at Ole Miss during James Meredith's integration, and his encounter with Dan Rather later.

segments.title: Outro
segments.summary: Hosts sign off and plug the show's platforms.
